AI tools for General contractors

General contractors coordinate other trades, which means documentation, scheduling and compliance are constant rather than occasional. On larger projects the paper trail is often contractually required, not merely useful.

Where General contractors work goes wrong

A GC's job is coordination, which means information rather than tools: subcontractor schedules, RFIs, inspection records and progress claims. When paperwork is missing, payments stop — regardless of how good the work is.

Frequently asked questions

Which tools for general contractors are worth trying first?

The three that stand out here are Togal.AI (Contractors who bid from plans and spend hours on manual takeoffs), Knowify (Contractors who need to know whether a job actually made money), Contractor Foreman (Small contractors who want one system instead of five spreadsheets). Start with the one that matches your size and the work you do most, not the one with the longest feature list.

How much does software for general contractors cost?

Across the 17 tools on this page, 5 have a free tier and the rest are paid, most of them billed per user per month. Prices move often, so confirm on the vendor site before committing.

Can I try these tools for free?

Yes 鈥?Expensify, ChatGPT, Claude, Otter.ai all have a free tier, so you can run a few real jobs through them before paying anything.

When does a GC outgrow spreadsheets?

Around three concurrent projects. Below that, spreadsheets work; beyond it, the number of subcontractor schedules, change orders and payment applications exceeds what you can track without a shared system.
